steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The AQA 8236 written paper is 1 hour 30 minutes and is worth 40% of the total GCSE grade

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Read all questions before starting — plan your time based on marks available per question

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Spend approximately 1.5 minutes per mark as a rough guide for timing

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always plan extended answers before writing — a brief outline saves time and improves structure

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How should you manage your time in the AQA 8236 written exam? | Q: What is the PEEL structure and why is it useful? | Q: How should you approach an annotation question?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Allocate approximately 1.5 minutes per mark. Read all questions first, then start with your strongest topic. For a 6-mark question, allow about 9 minutes including planning time. Leave 5 minutes at th | PEEL stands for Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link. It ensures each paragraph has a clear point, is supported by specific evidence from the work, explains how the evidence supports the point, and link | Use precise dance terminology — not vague labels. Place labels accurately on the correct part of the diagram. Cover action, dynamics, space and relationships where relevant, and ensure each annotation

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Read the whole paper first and mark up command words before writing anything Use the 1.5 minutes per mark rule — a 6-mark question gets 9 minutes maximum Plan extended answers with 3–4 key points before writing in full sentences Never leave a question blank — even a rough answer may pick up marks for knowledge Check that every paragraph links back to the question focus or choreographic intention
